newsitem.title: USA: Dime acquisition includes $150 mln goodwill.
newsitem.headline: Dime acquisition includes $150 mln goodwill.

text.p: Dime Bancorp Inc's planned acquisition of North American Mortgage Corp includes $150 million in goodwill which will be amortized over 15 years, president and chief executive Lawrence Toal said in a telephone interview Monday.
Earlier, the two firms announced Dime would acquire North American in a stock transaction valued at $374 million.
"This gets us where we want to be in terms of scale in the mortgage banking business," Toal said. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 1997.

"The deal is accretive to earnings on a GAAP (generally accepted accounting principles) and a cash basis," Fred Koons, chief executive of Dime's mortgage business, said during the same telephone interview. Koons will head the Dime mortgage business from a headquarters in Tampa, Fla.
Koons said Dime expects to achieve $18.8 million in cost savings in the acquisition, equivalent to about 7.5 percent of North American's total expense base.
Rich Mirro, who will be president and chief operating officer of the Dime mortgage business, said there will be some staff reduction at North American's California facilities.
Mirro did not provide any figures on the staff reductions North American is headquartered in Santa Rosa, Calif.
Koons said Dime is interested in expansion of B and C mortgage products aimed at the subprime market, an area which North American only recently started to roll out nationally.
He also said a "very attractive arrangement" in which North American originated the subprime loans and pre-sold them to ContiFinancial Corp is expected to continue.
Toal said North American's $8.3 billion in mortgage originations in the year ended March 31, and the combined $30 billion servicing portfolio, matches Dime's targets.
Terry Hodel, president of North American, will be vice chairman of the Dime mortgage business.

Toal said at the Dime shareholders meeting in May that the company is transforming itself from a traditional thrift into a supercommunity bank with emphasis in mortgage banking, consumer financial services, commercial real estate lending, consumer lending and business banking. Now that the mortgage business has been expanded, he said, Dime can concentrate on broadening the other areas.
Toal said the deal with North American came about after Dime initiated negotiations.

Dime was advised in the negotiations by Salomon Inc's Salomon Brothers and Bankers Trust New York Corp, Toal said, while North American was advised by Morgan Stanley & Co, a unit of Morgan Stanley Dean Witter Discover.
In the transaction, Dime is paying 1.79 times North American's book value calculated on March 31.
North American shareholders will receive 1.37 shares of Dime for each North American share, valuing the shares at $26.03 based on Dime's closing price Friday.
North American was up 7/8 to 24-1/8 Monday afternoon and Dime was off 3/4 to 18-1/4.
